guard_note: TP>1 guard with MoE router creation outside the RNG tracker fork; T01 already permits model-parallel RNG initialization as a precondition.
rationale: The router weight is replicated state that must be checksum-equal across the TP replication group at init, violated by unforked default-RNG construction.

guard_note: any-topology / fp32 no-ZeRO guard; T09's clip_coef clause is topology-agnostic.
rationale: The applied clip coefficient must equal max_norm/(global_norm+eps), and torch.max pins it to 1 so no clipping occurs — a clip-coefficient-vs-reference-recomputation violation.

guard_note: T11 already lists 'initial_lr present in restored param_groups' as a precondition; single-rank/any topology guard.
rationale: The LR/scheduler field restored after restart must equal its value at save, and a missing initial_lr key silently loses the peak LR.

guard_note: Guard is bf16-enabled-without-explicit-comm-dtype; T05 already constrains dtype(grad_communication) to the designated communication dtype.
rationale: The allreduce/reduce operand must carry the dtype the bf16 recipe designates, and the fp32 default silently violates the designated communication dtype at the collective's use point.

guard_note: single-rank/any guard; the non-designated writer is an eval-mode forward pass mutating a module attribute.
rationale: The module's dropout_p attribute must retain its value across a forward call that is not its designated writer, but the eval branch permanently zeroes the instance attribute.

guard_note: Guard is MoE group construction at init with world_size>1 and num_experts != ep_size; T18 permits init-phase construction-flag effectiveness.
rationale: The realized expert-parallel group size must equal the configured ep_size, but construction consumes num_experts, so the effective value diverges from the accepted config.

guard_note: PP>1 guard with gradient accumulation; T08 already permits micro-batch-count divisors.
rationale: The accumulated gradient must carry the 1/num_micro_batches normalization its spec mandates, and disabling loss_scale_by_gas without compensation leaves the gradient scaled by the accumulation count.

guard_note: DP>1 / ZeRO-2 backward guard is stated, but no defect mechanism or fix is given.
rationale: root_cause merely restates the title ('a regression makes grad norms lower'), naming no compared objects or defect site, so no relation can be derived from the whitelisted fields.

guard_note: ZeRO-1/2 CPU-offload guard extended to ga_steps==1 with multiple backward() calls per step — same precondition kind as T07's 'accumulation outside no_sync with CPU offloading'.
rationale: The accumulation buffer must equal the exact sum of every per-backward gradient contribution, but the ga_steps>1 gate drops the intermediate backward contributions.

guard_note: DP>1 guard, ZeRO-2 overlap_comm+contiguous_gradients — T10 already covers the shared ipg-buffer producer/consumer hazard.
rationale: The reduce consuming an ipg bucket must be ordered after the gradient writes that produced it, and the mistimed index reset lets reduce_ipg_grads read stale buffer contents.

guard_note: EP>1 guard; T28 already requires the partition id to be computed within each param group's own process group rather than one global DP world size.
rationale: Each rank's bit16 working partition must correspond elementwise to its own fp32 master partition, but a global-world-size partition computation mis-sizes MoE EP groups and leaves _hp_mapping unlinked.

guard_note: EP>1 guard; T08 already covers the expert-gradient divisor being the wrong (edp vs dp) world size.
rationale: The expert-gradient scale factor must equal the divisor its spec mandates, but the bf16 optimizer's MoE EP path is off by ep_size (with the wrong DP group used for partition/allreduce).

guard_note: single-rank/any guard; the oracle is the unfused/reference LayerNorm backward formula.
rationale: The computed gamma gradient must equal the value its reference backward formula mandates, but the kernel indexes gamma/beta with threadIdx.y instead of threadIdx.x.

guard_note: EP>1 guard at init; same construction-flag effectiveness kind T18 already permits.
rationale: The realized EP group count/size must equal the configured ep_size, but _create_ep_parallel_group is passed num_experts, yielding zero or malformed groups.

guard_note: EP>1 + DP>1 guard under CPU offload; the residual difference is the reduction operand's device, a precondition kind T09 already covers via its CPU-offload clipping precondition.
rationale: The applied MoE gradient norm must equal a reference recomputation over the actual gradients including the DP reduction, but averaging a CPU-resident norm tensor skips the cross-rank GPU reduction.

guard_note: DP>1 / ZeRO-3 guard; T05 already requires reduce-scatter and all-gather buffers to honor the configured communication_data_type.
rationale: Parameter/gradient communication buffers must carry the configured communication dtype at their use point, and ZeRO-3 ignores the configured value.

guard_note: DP>1 multi-node guard on the ZeRO-3 universal-checkpoint load path; T11 already permits universal-checkpoint preconditions.
rationale: Every restored state element must equal its value at save, but the multi-machine stage-3 universal load path restores values that make loss jump instead of resuming.

guard_note: single-rank/any guard, bf16+ZeRO-0 config-flag precondition — same kind as T11's existing bf16 load-path preconditions.
rationale: Optimizer moments and the step counter after load must equal their saved values, but the bf16+ZeRO-0 flag path silently drops them.

guard_note: any-topology guard, bf16+ZeRO-0 engine path — T07's buffer-zeroing clause already covers this precondition kind.
rationale: Accumulation must start from a zeroed buffer each step, but skipping zero_grad leaves the previous step's gradients summed into the current step's contributions.

guard_note: any-topology guard, multi-param-group optimizer at optimizer_step.
rationale: The obligation is one scalar LR entry per optimizer param group from the scheduler's output — a scheduler-output-to-param-group correspondence count whose objects match no frozen template (not T18's configured-vs-effective value, not T12/T26's inventories).

guard_note: single-rank/any guard, bf16+fp32_grad_accum without ZeRO; evidence is title-only (no root_cause), so the extraction is medium confidence.
rationale: The optimizer implementation made effective at init must equal the one the accepted bf16+fp32-grad-accum config selects, but BF16_Optimizer is chosen against that configuration.

guard_note: any/DP>1 guard, ZeRO-3 contiguous_gradients bucket-boundary precondition — same kind as T07's existing partial-bucket clauses.
rationale: Each per-parameter gradient contribution must be added exactly once into its designated reduction buffer, but the strict less-than bucket test drops a gradient that exactly fills the bucket.

guard_note: any-topology guard; T35's first precondition is exactly requires_grad=False parameters wrongly entering optimizer state.
rationale: Designated-frozen parameters must be excluded from every update channel, but they are placed into the optimizer's trainable groups.

guard_note: any/DP>1 guard, ZeRO-1/2 fp16 dynamic loss scaling at a scale-change step — a precondition kind T09 already admits.
rationale: The reported global grad norm must equal a reference recomputation over the actual gradients, but unscaling by the post-decay loss_scale rather than the prev_scale the gradients carry skews the norm used for clipping.

guard_note: single-rank/any guard, asymmetric int8 dequantize instantiated with T=float; T05 is the runner-up but the case states the output tensor's runtime dtype tag is correct, so no dtype signal can witness it.
rationale: The dequantized value must equal its reference dequantization for the requested output type, but a hard-coded __half round-trip truncates ~13 mantissa bits inside an otherwise correctly-typed fp32 output.

guard_note: DP>1 multi-node guard; the residual difference is the rank-keying of the restored slice, matching T11's per-rank exact-shard restore preconditions.
rationale: Each rank's restored partition must equal the slice it saved, but narrowing by local_rank makes ranks on different nodes load the same offset, so half the parameters restore the wrong slice.

guard_note: DP>1 guard, ZeRO-2 overlap_comm+contiguous_gradients — T10 already carries the compute-stream-waits-on-reduction-stream ipg clause.
rationale: The backward write into the swapped ipg bucket must be ordered after the in-flight reduce reading the aliased flat allocation completes, and no cross-stream wait enforces it.

guard_note: DP>1 guard, ZeRO++ hierarchical partition with stage-3 prefetch — same async-copy-before-consumption hazard kind T10 permits.
rationale: The prefetch all-gather consuming ds_secondary_tensor must be ordered after the asynchronous partition copy that produces it, but no stream synchronization is recorded, so the gather broadcasts pre-copy contents.

guard_note: any/DP>1 guard, bf16 optimizer hp-accumulation path — same buffer-clearing precondition kind T07 already covers.
rationale: Each micro-batch gradient must enter the high-precision accumulation exactly once from a cleared low-precision buffer, but leaving lp_grads uncleared lets a contribution be counted again.

guard_note: DP>1 and PP>1 guard; T01 already covers tied word-embedding replicas across pipeline stages under the distributed optimizer.
rationale: The tied embedding gradient copies must agree across their replication group, but reduce-scattering before the cross-stage all-reduce leaves wte and lm_head partials on different DP ranks and summed incorrectly.

guard_note: TP>1 guard with MoE router construction under the default CUDA RNG; T01 permits model-parallel RNG initialization.
rationale: The unsharded router weight is replicated state that must be checksum-equal across the TP group, but default-RNG construction makes it diverge from initialization and changes routing decisions per rank.

guard_note: TP>1 guard with vocab_size not divisible by the TP degree — the same non-divisibility precondition kind T03 already lists for sequence length.
rationale: Loss must be invariant (within tolerance) to the TP degree, which is a performance-only knob, but uneven vocab splits make loss diverge systematically from the single-GPU reference.

guard_note: any-topology guard; T26's precondition 'activation recompute re-running router forward' is exactly this case.
rationale: The aux-loss tracker increment must occur exactly once per step, but --moe-layer-recompute runs the router forward twice so the load-balancing (and z-) loss is accumulated twice.

guard_note: EP>1 guard; the padding source is MoE pad_to_capacity dummy tokens rather than dataset padding — the same padding-position guard kind.
rationale: Padded positions must contribute zero to the loss, but dummy capacity-padding tokens enter the routing map feeding the load-balancing loss, pinning it at 1.0 regardless of true token distribution.

guard_note: single-rank/any guard, precision-aware optimizer with CPU offload — a precondition kind T11 admits; the evidence isolates the failing sub-state as optimizer state.
rationale: Optimizer state after load must equal its value at save, but serialization/deserialization under CPU offload corrupts it, making loss jump from 0.31 to 10 on resume.

guard_note: PP>1 guard with virtual pipelining and num_layers not divisible by pp_size*vp_size — the same partition-map precondition kind T32 covers.
rationale: The realized layer-to-stage assignment must equal the partition the pipeline config mandates, but integer division silently covers only 64 of the configured 80 layers.

guard_note: CP>1 guard; T08 already permits cp_size in the specified normalization factor and micro-batch-count divisors.
rationale: The MTP loss gradient must carry the divisor its spec mandates, but MTPLossAutoScaler ignores the cp_size multiplication applied to num_microbatches, under-scaling by the CP factor.

guard_note: single-rank/any guard; the non-designated writer is the eval-mode forward pass.
rationale: The module's dropout_p must retain its value across an eval forward that is not its designated writer, but the instance attribute is set to 0 permanently, disabling dropout in all later training steps.

guard_note: any/EP>1 guard, bf16 recipe with sigmoid router scoring — same designated-fp32-router-path precondition kind as T05's expert_bias clause.
rationale: The router scoring path is designated fp32 under the bf16 mixed-precision recipe, but the sigmoid is computed on bf16 logits, so the routing scores lose their designated precision at the use point.

guard_note: Megatron-FSDP precision-aware FusedAdam is a precondition guard not listed among T28's permitted preconditions, but is the same guard kind (mixed-precision master/working sync point).
rationale: FusedAdam's own master_weights duplicate is never refreshed from Megatron-FSDP's main weights, so the working parameter no longer equals the cast of its designated master partition at the post-step sync point.

guard_note: bf16 main_params_dtype with use_precision_aware_optimizer and no FP8 is a precondition guard of the same kind as T28's listed mixed-precision master-creation guards.
rationale: The mis-gated master_weights condition leaves two independently managed master copies, so the working parameter is not the elementwise cast of the master partition that actually owns the high-precision values.

guard_note: sigmoid score_function with expert_bias (aux-loss-free routing) extends T04's routing-spec preconditions; same guard kind.
rationale: Adding expert_bias to raw logits before the sigmoid makes the realized router score deviate from the routing specification's post-sigmoid bias-adjusted score on identical inputs.

guard_note: expert_tensor_parallel_size != tensor_model_parallel_size with average_in_collective is a precondition guard of the same kind as T08's listed ep_size!=dp_size expert-divisor guard.
rationale: The expert gradient carries 1/(ep_size*edp_size) instead of the specified 1/dp_size normalization factor when DP != EDP.

guard_note: moe_router_topk==1 with post-topk softmax is already a listed T17 precondition.
rationale: Softmax over a length-1 topk tensor is constant, so the router weight on the active loss path receives an identically zero gradient.

guard_note: tensor_model_parallel_size>1 with MoE aux loss matches T08's listed TP-factor aux-loss guard.
rationale: The aux-loss coefficient omits the 1/tp_size divisor, so the post-all-reduce aux-loss gradient carries a tp_size factor the specification does not mandate.

guard_note: ChainedOptimizer resume under EP>1 extends T11's listed ChainedOptimizer sub-optimizer restore precondition; same guard kind.
rationale: After load the outer optimizer's param_groups remain a detached derived cache that was not refreshed to match the restored inner-optimizer primaries, so LR state no longer equals the restored value.

guard_note: fp32 logits making .float() a no-op alias is a precondition guard of the same kind as T23's listed in-place-clobber guards.
rationale: The in-place subtraction mutates the very tensor saved for autograd, an operation that is not a designated writer of the saved activation.

guard_note: CUDA-graph replay with aliased input/output buffers extends T23's listed graph-capture buffer guards; same guard kind.
rationale: The unconditional copy_ into an aliased cudagraph_input overwrites a value a preceding op wrote in place, mutating state the replay node is not the designated writer of.

guard_note: FP4 (config.fp4 without config.fp8) with selective recompute is already the guard kind listed in T24's FP4 MoE recompute precondition.
rationale: The FP8-only gate leaves the FP4-quantized tensor cached, so the recomputed attention forward does not reproduce the original bf16 forward within the same step.

guard_note: CP>1 with a HybridEP dispatcher is a topology guard of the same kind as T25's listed PP>1 and CP>1 / SP>1 guards.
rationale: Per-CP-rank shard offsets padded to 32 violate the HybridEP dispatcher kernel's 128-element alignment contract, so loads/stores cross token boundaries.

guard_note: softmax_auxiliary_loss with gradient accumulation matches T08's listed z-loss batch_size_in_tokens guard verbatim.
rationale: The z-loss divides by num_micro_batches instead of the specified batch_size_in_tokens normalization factor.

guard_note: activation checkpointing with dropout>0 is already a listed T24 precondition.
rationale: The inverted preserve_rng_state condition makes the recomputed forward draw a different dropout mask than the original forward within the same step.
root_cause merely restates the title ('incomplete or incorrect') and names no defect or fix, so the fields cannot discriminate a save-inventory count relation from a restored-value equality relation.

The obligation is that a constructed QK-norm module's size equal the dimension implied by the configured n_kv_heads/n_heads under GQA — a derived config-vs-construction consistency that no frozen template's objects cover (not a parallel-layout contract, not an init statistic, not a single configured knob's effective value).

guard_note: fused-vs-native cross-entropy implementation selection is a precondition guard of the same kind as T03's listed attention-backend-selection guard.
rationale: The fused loss variant must produce the same loss as the same computation under the native (compiled) baseline configuration on identical inputs, and it was consistently lower.

relation_operator: reference_equivalence (reported MFU vs true device peak FLOPS)
rationale: The violated quantity is a hard-coded hardware datasheet constant; the training trace carries no signal that witnesses a 2x-low peak (training is unaffected and inflated MFU need not exceed 100%).

guard_note: init_fn='normal' branch on multi-layer models extends T27's listed depth-scaled-init preconditions; same guard kind.
rationale: The post-init division by sqrt(2*n_layers) leaves ff_out's realized std a factor 1/sqrt(2L) below the configured init_std spec.

guard_note: resume past the first epoch with max_epochs>1 is a precondition guard of the same kind as T11's listed resume guards.
rationale: Restart folds the epoch into the base seed and reshuffle then increments it again — a transformation re-applied on load — so the restored shuffle RNG state does not equal the state the original run held at that epoch.

guard_note: matches T08's listed masked-mean z-loss guard verbatim.
rationale: Dividing z_squared by mask.mean() applies a normalization factor other than the specified masked mean over valid positions.

guard_note: FSDP collect_param_metrics combining sums/norms/numels in one reduction is a precondition guard of the same kind as T09's listed metric-recording guards.
rationale: Concatenating and splitting on the wrong axis makes the logged per-parameter reduction metrics disagree with a reference recomputation over the actual parameters and gradients.

guard_note: metrics_log_interval>1 with clipping enabled extends T18's precondition list; same guard kind (accepted knob vs effective value).
rationale: The clipping helpers hard-code collect_param_metrics=True, so the runtime-effective metrics-collection cadence does not equal the accepted configured value.

guard_note: cosine-then-linear-final-decay concatenation is a precondition guard of the same kind as T04's listed LR-schedule reference-curve guards.
rationale: The final segment's start/end factors (1.0 to alpha_f instead of alpha_f to alpha_f**2) make the realized LR deviate from the closed-form reference curve, spiking back to base LR at the handoff.

guard_note: embedding init with a d_model-dependent scale factor matches T27's listed embedding fan_in / embed_scale guard.
rationale: Omitting the sqrt(d_model) factor leaves the realized embedding init std 16x below the spec std at initialization.

guard_note: single-rank flash-attn kernel layout contract is a topology guard value not listed for T25 (all listed values are >1 parallel degrees), but the same guard kind — T25's schema already covers op_contract layouts.
rationale: The tensor handed to flash_attn carries (B,H,S,D) where the kernel's contract mandates (B,S,H,D), so the layout an operation touches does not equal its expected layout.

relation_operator: count_frequency_match (model context length vs tokenized example length)
rationale: The runtime-expressible obligation is that the model's max_sequence_length cover the length the data was tokenized at so no example is silently truncated; T18 cannot express it (the wrong value IS the accepted config and is honored) and T34's counted object is the example budget against the step plan, not per-example sequence extent.

guard_note: isinstance/variable-name init dispatch reaching the wrong module matches the guard kind of T27's listed init-dispatch preconditions.
rationale: The typo initializes ff_out twice and never applies the designated init to ff_proj, whose statistics therefore do not conform to the configured init spec.

guard_note: modulo-2^16 truncation of token ids is the same guard kind as T06's listed uint16-reader-vs-uint32-storage preconditions.
rationale: Token ids are reinterpreted through a 16-bit width that cannot represent the tokenizer's vocabulary, so the ids consumed do not equal the ids stored.

guard_note: Transformer.apply_activation_checkpointing with nn.Dropout present matches T24's listed activation-checkpointing-with-dropout precondition.
rationale: The hard-coded preserve_rng_state=False makes the backward recompute draw a fresh dropout mask, so the re-executed forward does not equal the original execution.

guard_note: AdamW maintaining state['step'] matches T15's listed step-counter precondition.
rationale: The commented-out step.add_ stalls the optimizer step counter at its initial value, so it never advances by its defined increment and bias correction stays permanently wrong.

guard_note: non-fused RotaryEmbedding in packed mode with cu_doc_lens matches T16's listed precondition verbatim.
rationale: Positions computed as a global arange ignore document boundaries, so the applied rotary encoding does not equal the spec encoding of each token's intended intra-document position.

guard_note: loader-internal plus trainer-level increment of the same counter is a precondition guard of the same kind as T26's listed tracker-increment-once guards.
rationale: tokens_processed is advanced both inside __iter__ and by the trainer, so the increment event fires twice per batch boundary instead of exactly once and resume skips twice the data.

guard_note: ComplexRotaryEmbedding is a module-variant precondition guard of the same kind as T16's listed non-fused packed-mode rotary guard.
rationale: The complex-RoPE path never accepts cu_doc_lens, so the applied rotary phase follows the global token index rather than each token's intended per-document position.

guard_note: PP>1 with max_grad_norm matches T09's listed cross-PP-stage L2-reduction precondition and permitted PP>1 topology guard.
rationale: The clip uses a per-stage local norm without the square/all-reduce/sqrt combination across PP ranks, so the applied clip coefficient does not equal a reference recomputation over all contributing gradients.

guard_note: FlashAttn closed-interval window semantics matches T18's listed sliding-window off-by-one precondition; T30 is the runner-up because a too-large window does place mass on forbidden positions.
rationale: Passing window_size into flash-attn's closed-interval window makes the realized per-row attention extent window_size+1, not the configured window size.

guard_note: nested source_group_size on both the inner source and outer packing config is a precondition guard of the same kind as T18's listed config-merge guards.
rationale: The two settings compose multiplicatively, so the runtime-effective grouping is 64 documents per group rather than the configured 8.

guard_note: BLT debias with a low-probability logprob tail is a precondition guard of the same kind as T04's listed analytic-formula guards.
rationale: log(sum(exp(logprobs))) underflows to log(0) = -inf instead of equaling the stable log-sum-exp reference the debias term specifies on the same inputs.
